summary.intent: Understand the memory loop architecture deeply, then design and implement an MCP server that allows Claude to pull memories on demand as a complement to hook-based push injection.
summary.outcome: Full MCP server implementation shipped across 4 commits: `entire mcp-server` command with `search_memories` and `save_memory` tools, hook installation extended to write `mcpServers.entire` to `.claude/settings.json`, and 18 new passing tests.

repo: Memory loop has two independent controls: `mode` (off/manual/auto) controls hook injection, `activation_policy` (review/auto) controls whether generated memories auto-activate.
`manual` mode means no hook injection but full CLI/TUI access — not 'manually trigger injection'. This is considered misleading by the user.
Refresh (backfill summaries → backfill facets → pattern analysis → generation → reconciliation) is always manual; `auto` mode only controls injection.

Facets are structured metadata (repeated instructions, missing context signals, friction points, skill opportunities, repo/workflow learnings) extracted from summaries and used as input to pattern analysis.
Injection gate (`passesInjectionGate`) requires `StatusActive` — candidates, suppressed, and archived records never inject via hooks.

`AddManualRecord` sets `Status: StatusActive` for CLI-created records; MCP-created memories should use `StatusCandidate` to require human review — requires bypassing `AddManualRecord` or overriding status.
Pre-existing uncommitted changes in `skilldb/cache.go`, `skilldb/cache_test.go`, `skilltui/picker.go`, `skilltui/root.go` cause test failures unrelated to this work.
Subagents committed their own work incrementally; main session committed hooks/command changes separately.
`t.Parallel()` cannot be combined with `t.Chdir()` in Go tests — causes a panic.

code.finding: Injection gate: if mode != ModeAuto, maybeInjectMemoryLoop exits immediately. No manual injection path exists.
fingerprintForRecord and makeRecordID were unexported; had to export as FingerprintForRecord and MakeRecordID for use in the MCP save_memory handler.
InstallHooks already had high maintidx lint score before MCP changes — pre-existing issue, not introduced by this work.

workflow: Subagent-driven development pattern: dispatch implementer agents per task, verify tests after each, commit incrementally.
Hook-based injection is a push model (fires before Claude sees anything); MCP tools are a pull model (Claude calls them during conversation when it decides it needs context).
MCP server mode gating should check mode on every tool call, not just at startup, so mode changes take effect immediately without restarting the server.
For MCP search that needs to bypass the injection gate (to return candidates too), a separate filtering+scoring path is needed rather than reusing `SelectRelevant`/`PreviewSelection` directly.
The staging file pattern (write IDs to file, hook reads and deletes on next turn) was considered for manual injection but rejected as too clunky — MCP tool approach preferred.

friction: The `entire mcp-server` cobra command initially had an unused `cmd` parameter that triggered a lint error.
`PreviewSelection` is too restrictive for MCP search (filters out candidates, returns empty on empty query) — required a custom scoring path in the handler.
Background test task notification arrived after the session concluded, requiring a retroactive explanation that the failure was pre-existing.
User interrupted the assistant mid-response twice, requiring 'continue' prompts to resume.
Finding the exact location of `UninstallHooks` required multiple grep attempts with different patterns.
open_items: Consider removing `manual` mode entirely and simplifying to `off`/`auto` — user agreed it's misleading and `auto`+`activation_policy:review` covers the safe on-ramp use case.
TUI `i` keybinding to stage/inject a selected memory was mentioned but not implemented.
`--local-dev` flag for `entire enable` (using `go run` instead of binary for the MCP server entry) was mentioned in testing instructions but may not exist yet.
Pre-existing `skilldb` test failures need investigation and resolution.
The `InstallHooks` function maintidx lint issue is pre-existing but worth addressing separately.
